title: Will CXMT take  over micron in 2030?
gist: A SemiWiki forum repost of a July 24 Reuters investigation showing that China's ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) has become powerful enough to raise DRAM prices on Huawei and refuse relief, culminating in CXMT expelling engineers from Huawei-linked equipment vendor SiCarrier from its Hefei R&D cleanrooms in June. CXMT is now the world's fourth-biggest memory maker, signed a previously unreported five-year ByteDance deal worth more than $7 billion, and together with YMTC is racing toward IPOs while the Pentagon has designated both as Chinese military companies. Note: the forum thread title asks about Micron in 2030, but the text never mentions Micron.

insights.claim: ChangXin Memory Technologies repeatedly raised prices on Huawei for months and held firm when Huawei demanded relief, according to two people familiar with the matter.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A domestic Chinese supplier out-negotiating Huawei signals that memory scarcity now overrides national-champion political hierarchy — supportive of sustained DRAM pricing.
insights.quote: For months, Chinese chip manufacturer ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) had been hiking prices on Huawei, one of the country's biggest technology companies.

insights.claim: In June, CXMT ordered engineers from Huawei-linked chipmaking-equipment vendor SiCarrier to pack their tools and leave its core R&D cleanrooms in Hefei, Anhui province without warning, and they have not been allowed back into the R&D zone.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Concrete evidence that China's semiconductor national team is fracturing into competing commercial interests, which slows the coordinated domestic toolchain buildout.
insights.quote: Without warning, CXMT ordered the engineers, who had been helping with equipment maintenance, to pack their tools and ‌leave the factory floor immediately
insights.locator: "The standoff came to a head on CXMT's factory floor in June."

insights.claim: Executives at SiCarrier concluded the cleanroom expulsion was the result of a power struggle between CXMT and Huawei, though the companies still do business with each other.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Intra-China supply-chain friction is a real constraint on Huawei's vertically integrated chip ambitions and on SiCarrier's access to production learning.
insights.quote: Executives at the Huawei-connected equipment vendor, SiCarrier, concluded the confrontation was the result of the power struggle between CXMT and Huawei

insights.claim: CXMT has risen to become the world's fourth-biggest maker of memory, including the DRAM used in smartphones, laptops and servers.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A fourth global DRAM supplier changes the oligopoly math that underpins memory cycle bull cases for the incumbent Korean and US producers.
insights.quote: CXMT has risen to become the world's fourth-biggest maker of memory, including the DRAM variety used in smartphones, laptops and servers.

insights.claim: The global buildout of AI data centers converted memory from a low-margin commodity into one of the world's most sought-after products, sparking pricing battles and a scramble for supply.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Identifies the mechanism behind the memory upcycle: AI capex, not device demand, is what re-rated the asset class.
insights.quote: the global buildout of AI data centers has transformed the humble components into one of the world's most sought-after products, sparking battles over pricing and a scramble for supply
insights.locator: "Memory chips that help devices run apps"

insights.claim: Chinese memory makers are now picking their clients and dictating prices, in some cases charging more than larger South Korean rivals Samsung and SK Hynix as Chinese buyers are forced to pay ever-higher prices.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Chinese memory selling above Korean pricing inverts the standard assumption that Chinese entrants deflate markets — near-term supportive for global memory ASPs.
insights.quote: In some cases, they are charging more than their larger South Korean rivals, Samsung and SK Hynix
insights.locator: "The Chinese memory makers are now picking clients"

insights.claim: CXMT signed a previously unreported five-year agreement with ByteDance this month worth more than $7 billion, according to three people familiar with the arrangement.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A multi-year, multi-billion-dollar domestic offtake locks in CXMT capacity ahead of its IPO and removes that volume from the merchant market.
insights.quote: CXMT this month signed a five-year agreement with ByteDance, TikTok's Chinese owner, worth more than $7 billion
insights.locator: "CXMT this month signed a five-year agreement"

insights.claim: CXMT and flash-memory counterpart YMTC spent years relying on government funding and racking up losses before AI demand made them profitable price-setters.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: The state-subsidized loss phase is what bought the capacity now being monetized — a template for how Chinese entrants convert subsidy into pricing power.
insights.quote: CXMT and its flash-memory counterpart, Yangtze Memory Technologies Corp, or YMTC, spent years relying on government funding and racking up losses.
insights.locator: "Memory chips that help devices run apps"

insights.claim: CXMT and YMTC, known in China as the twin stars of memory, are both racing toward blockbuster IPOs.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Two large memory IPOs would give China domestically funded expansion capital independent of state budgets — a structural threat to the memory oligopoly's capacity discipline.
insights.quote: both companies – known in China as the "twin stars" of memory – race toward blockbuster IPOs
insights.locator: "This account of how CXMT and YMTC are wielding"

insights.claim: The Chinese memory makers' grip on chip supply is putting them on a collision course with Washington as US scrutiny of their market power grows.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Escalating restrictions on Chinese memory are a live policy risk that would tighten global memory supply further rather than loosen it.
insights.quote: The Chinese companies' grip on chip supply is putting them on a collision course with Washington.
insights.locator: "Neither chipmaker responded to requests for comment"

insights.claim: The Pentagon has designated both CXMT and YMTC as Chinese military companies for their alleged role in China's military-civil fusion strategy, a charge both deny.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: The designation is the legal predicate for broader sanctions — a specific escalation trigger to monitor for memory supply and for buyers dependent on Chinese DRAM.
insights.quote: The Pentagon has designated ⁠both firms as Chinese military companies for what it says is their role in aiding China's military-civil fusion strategy — a charge they deny.
insights.locator: "The Chinese companies' grip on chip supply"

insights.claim: YMTC is already on the US Entity List, which has restricted its access to US-origin suppliers, software and tools used in memory-chip production, while CXMT is not similarly listed.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: The asymmetry between YMTC and CXMT is the actionable gap: adding CXMT to the Entity List would be the single largest supply shock available to US policymakers in DRAM.
insights.quote: YMTC is already on the U.S. Entity List, a designation that has restricted its access to U.S.-origin suppliers, software and tools used in memory-chip production.

insights.claim: The Reuters account is built on interviews with more than a dozen executives, engineers, suppliers and US officials plus a review of 50 Chinese government policy documents and company disclosures, which is unusually deep sourcing on opaque Chinese memory firms.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Sourcing depth raises the reliability weight to place on these pricing and contract details, which are otherwise unobtainable from public filings.
insights.quote: based on interviews with more than a dozen people, including executives, engineers, suppliers and U.S. officials, and a Reuters review of 50 Chinese government policy documents and company disclosures
insights.locator: "This account of how CXMT and YMTC are wielding their newfound clout"

insights.claim: Public information on SiCarrier is very rare, so any operational detail about the Huawei-linked equipment vendor carries outsized information value.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: SiCarrier is the key unknown in China's domestic toolchain — scarce disclosures like this are the only way to gauge how far Chinese equipment substitution has progressed.
insights.quote: News on SiCarrier is very rare.
insights.locator: Forum comment preceding the Reuters text
